donationTaxCredit.title: Donation Tax Credit Calculator
donationTaxCredit.subtitle: Donations made in {year} (settled the following January) · applies the separate limits and rates for political, special, general and religious donations to show how much tax you actually save
donationTaxCredit.salaryHint: Annual pay minus non-taxable allowances such as meal allowance. Donation limits are based on earned income, i.e. this amount minus the earned income deduction.

gifts.title: Annual donations by recipient
gifts.hint: Amounts paid from January to December {year}. For regular giving, use the monthly amount × 12. Include donations made by your spouse, children and parents.

political.label: Political donations
political.hint: Party dues, support associations of lawmakers and candidates, deposits with the election commission. Only donations in your own name count. Up to 100,000 KRW comes back almost in full.

special.label: Special donations
special.hint: Central and local government, national defense funds, disaster relief, facility and scholarship funds for private schools and national university hospitals, the Community Chest of Korea, etc. Creditable up to your earned income.

general.label: General donations (non-religious)
general.hint: Regular giving to social welfare foundations, public-interest corporations, civic groups, international relief charities, etc. Creditable up to 30% of earned income (after special donations).

religious.label: General donations (religious)
religious.hint: Offerings to churches, cathedrals, temples and other religious bodies. Up to 10% of earned income (after special donations), and 30% together with non-religious donations.

hometown.text: Hometown Love donations have different rates (in full up to 100,000 KRW, 40% up to 200,000 KRW), so they are calculated separately.

status.none: Enter your donations to see how much you get back.
status.noTax: You owe no tax to begin with, so there is nothing to reduce. Uncredited special and general donations may be carried forward for 10 years.
status.standard: The 130,000 KRW standard tax credit beats the donation credit ({donation} KRW), so special and general donations do not lower your tax. Political donations are credited on top of the standard credit.
status.partial: You only owe {tax} KRW, so that is all that can be saved. Unused special and general donation credits may be carried forward for 10 years.
status.swap: You get a {credit} KRW credit but lose the 130,000 KRW standard credit you had before, so your tax falls by {saving} KRW.
status.full: The {credit} KRW credit plus 10% local income tax comes off your tax in full.

bracket.title: Special + general credited amount (15% up to 10M KRW)
bracket.under: {left} KRW left until 10M KRW. Anything above that gets 30%.

table.caption: Limits and creditable amounts by donation type
table.excessNote: The {excess} KRW over the limit is not credited this year. General donations over the limit can be carried forward for 10 years.
table.note: Limits are based on earned income of {income} KRW. The general donation limit is filled by non-religious donations first (the total matches the statutory formula).

guide.title: Limits and credit rates by donation type (donations made in 2026)

rows.examples: Party dues, support associations of lawmakers and candidates, election commission deposits (in your own name)
rows.rate: 100/110 up to 100,000 KRW, 15% above (25% on the part over 30M KRW)

rows.examples: Central and local government, national defense funds and troop comfort gifts, disaster relief, facility and scholarship funds for private schools and national university hospitals, the Community Chest of Korea
rows.rate: 15%, 30% on the part of special + general over 10M KRW

rows.examples: Social welfare foundations, public-interest corporations, civic groups, international relief charities, etc.
rows.rate: 15%, 30% on the part of special + general over 10M KRW

rows.examples: Churches, cathedrals, temples and other religious bodies
rows.limit: 10% of (earned income − special donations) + the smaller of 20% and non-religious donations
rows.rate: 15%, 30% on the part of special + general over 10M KRW

rows.examples: A local government other than where you are registered
rows.rate: 100/110 up to 100,000 KRW, 40% up to 200,000 KRW, 15% above — see the hometown donation calculator

tips.title: Easy to miss
items: Religious donations are often missing from the simplified year-end data. Get a donation receipt from your religious body in January and hand it to your employer.

Donations made by your spouse, children and parents count too. Age does not matter, only the income test (income of 1M KRW or less, or gross pay of 5M KRW or less with only earned income). Donations by a family member claimed as a dependant by someone else do not count.
Only political donations in your own name are credited. Political donations in a family member's name are excluded.
Special and general donations not credited because they exceeded the limit or your tax ran out can be carried forward for 10 years. Carried-forward amounts are credited before that year's donations.
The 40% rate (an extra 10 points on the part over 30M KRW) applied only to donations made in 2024. For donations made in 2026, the top rate is 30% on the part over 10M KRW.
The donation credit is a special tax credit, so it cannot be combined with the 130,000 KRW standard credit. Political and Hometown Love donations are credited on top of the standard credit.
